events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.60)
events.body:
The dispute type filed is no_show, and the timeline is settled by system records: accepted 08:40:00, driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:44:40 40 m from the pickup, stayed within 200 m and stationary until cancelling at 08:50:20, which is 5 min 40 s of waiting counted from arrival [F4][F6][F7][F3]. Before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 08:45) and made 1 in-app call (08:46) [F5][F10][F11][F13]. The fee on record is $5.00 [F4][F8]. On those ✓ elements NS-1 (i)–(iii) are satisfied and no NS-9 repeat-rider flag arises (0 prior no-shows in 30 days) [F18][NS-1][NS-9].

That would leave only the NS-0 reading of why he cancelled: the app reason is rider_no_show, and his own words are "waited more than 5 minutes at the pickup. No rider, so I cancelled" [F4][F11][F14]. Those words give no reason of his own (no car trouble, personal matter, other job, refusal of the trip) — they are exactly the no-show account NS-1 already tests — so the element reads met and NS-1 would hold the $5.00 fee [F10][F11][F14][NS-0][NS-1].

However, the rider's complaint also states that when she called the driver back about the charge "he kept making comments about my body and asked where I live. I felt very uncomfortable" [complaint, F4 context]. That is an allegation of sexual/harassing remarks and of being made to feel unsafe, aimed at the rider, arising out of this trip. Even though the chat and driver statement themselves contain no safety content [F10][F11][F14], the screen is on every case and any text in the file counts, so this allegation must be screened [SAFE-1]. Because such an allegation is present, the case is a safety case and I may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome — I can only summarise it for the human reviewer [SAFE-1][SAFE-2][SAFE-3]. That obligation displaces the otherwise applicable no_action on the no-show fee.

The record does contain the settled no-show elements (arrival, ≥5 min wait, message plus call, continuous presence, rider not at pickup, no GPS gap), so the dispute is decidable on the fare facts; but nothing in the record lets me assess the post-cancellation allegation (no call recording on record [F13]), and a safety screen with a suspected concern is the reason for escalation, not a missing record about the fare. Confidence is moderate because the safety allegation rests on the rider's account alone, but a possible harassment allegation is precisely what must go to a person [SAFE-3].
